areas.name: Laxmi Road
areas.known_for: Pune's traditional shopping street - sarees, clothing, jewellery and festival shopping.
areas.notes: The old city's main commercial axis through the peths; its side lanes lead into Tulsi Baug and Raviwar Peth. Long-running saree houses here include Moolchand Mill (see standout shops).

areas.name: Tulsi Baug
areas.known_for: A bargain bazaar grown around the Peshwa-era Ram temple complex; the name means "basil garden".
areas.best_for: Budget clothing, kitchenware, puja items, accessories
areas.notes: Five lanes of dense stalls; haggling is the norm. The Tulshibaug Ram Mandir, built under the Peshwas, stands inside.

sources.label: Times of India: Bargains galore at Tulshibaug

areas.name: Mahatma Phule Mandai
areas.known_for: The 1886 Gothic market building - the city's biggest vegetable and fruit market.
areas.best_for: Fresh produce, dried fruit and spice stalls around it
areas.notes: Built as Reay Market; mornings are the busiest. A landmark in its own right - see the history timeline.

areas.name: Raviwar Peth and Sonya Maruti Chowk
areas.known_for: Pune's jewellery quarter - gold and silver shops run by the same families for five or six generations.
areas.best_for: Gold and silver jewellery, old-style designs
areas.notes: Several jewellers here trace back over a century, including P. N. Gadgil & Sons, featured in the Indian Express "Postcards from the Past" series. Ranka Jewellers (1879) is a few lanes away on Tilak Road.

areas.name: Juna Bazaar
areas.known_for: A weekly flea market for antiques, brassware, old cameras, vinyl and curios - Pune's own "chor bazaar".
areas.notes: Held on Wednesdays and Sundays, roughly 9 am to 5 pm, per current listings. The Times of India calls it a 250-year-old market.

areas.name: Hong Kong Lane
areas.known_for: A compact street-shopping lane for bags, footwear, phone accessories and books near Garware Bridge.
areas.notes: A small, dense lane; combine with the street stalls along FC Road.

areas.name: Fergusson College Road
areas.known_for: Street stalls for clothing and accessories along the pavement, alongside cafes and bookshops.
areas.notes: Street shopping concentrates on the stalls between Deccan Gymkhana and Shivajinagar; r/pune threads routinely name FC Road for street shopping.

sources.label: r/pune: Street shopping areas in Pune

areas.name: MG Road and East Street
areas.known_for: The Cantonment's heritage shopping streets - Irani and Parsi-era shops, bakeries and old restaurants among the retail.
areas.best_for: Iconic food institutions (see standout shops), general retail
areas.notes: Walk East Street for Kayani Bakery and the old Camp storefronts; Fashion Street, a lane of export-surplus clothing stalls, sits off MG Road.

sources.label: Travel + Leisure Asia: Pune shopping destinations

shops.name: P. N. Gadgil & Sons
shops.known_for: Gold and silver jewellery from a house whose founding is traced to 1832.
shops.note: The Gadgil family began the business in 1832 (starting in Sangli, per the company record) and its Pune shops in the Raviwar Peth-Laxmi Road quarter have served generations; the Indian Express "Postcards from the Past" profiles the house.

sources.label: Indian Express: Postcards from the Past

shops.name: Ranka Jewellers
shops.known_for: Gold jewellery from a Pune family business started in 1879.
shops.note: The Ranka family traces its jewellery business in Pune to 1879; the company records Shri Pukhraj Ranka re-establishing it, and seven generations have since run it. Now a multi-store group, with the Tilak Road shop the original.

shops.name: International Book Service
shops.note: Opened in 1931 beside the Deccan Gymkhana post office and among the city's oldest bookshops; the Times of India notes letters from Jawaharlal Nehru on its walls.

shops.name: Express Book Service
shops.known_for: Heritage English bookshop in the Cantonment.
shops.note: Hindustan Times (2017) lists Express Book Service among Pune's surviving old bookstores at over 80 years old; an exact founding year is not published, so none is claimed.

shops.name: Akshardhara Book Gallery
shops.known_for: Long-running Marathi bookshop in the old city.
shops.note: A Bajirao Road institution for Marathi books; Hindustan Times (2017) lists it among the city's surviving heritage bookstores.

shops.name: Moolchand Mill
shops.known_for: Multi-storey saree emporium on the old shopping street.
shops.note: LBB Pune lists Moolchand Mill as one of the oldest and best-known saree shops on Laxmi Road; the founding year is not published, so none is claimed.

shops.name: Kalashetram Silks
shops.known_for: Paithani sarees - Pune's specialist name for the weave.
shops.note: Named in curated Paithani guides (WedMeGood) as a Pune specialist for the weave; treated as a local-known specialist rather than a dated institution.

shops.name: Dorabjee & Sons
shops.known_for: Parsi food, especially dhansak, in a near-unchanged old-world dining room.
shops.note: Founded by Sorabjee Dorabjee in 1878 and run today by the fourth generation; the Indian Express documents a menu kept essentially the same since 1878.

shops.name: Kaka Halwai Sweet Centre
shops.known_for: Classic Maharashtrian mithai - pedha, kaju katli, anjir barfi.
shops.note: Founded by Kakasaheb Gadve in 1892; Loksatta and the family record trace the shop from a single Budhwar Peth unit to a citywide name.

shops.name: Gujar Cold Drink House
shops.known_for: Sharbat and sodas since the 1920s; later an early mastani stop.
shops.note: Established in 1923 by Baburao Gujar; the Indian Express's history of mastani begins at its counter.

sources.label: Indian Express: Know Your City - Mastani

shops.name: Cafe Goodluck
shops.known_for: Irani-cafe staples - bun maska, Irani chai, caramel custard.
shops.note: Set up by Hussain Ali Yakhshi in 1935; one of Pune's oldest Irani cafes, documented by Sahapedia and its own record.

shops.name: Poona Guest House
shops.known_for: Old-style Maharashtrian snacks and meals in a 1930s boarding house.
shops.note: Established by Nanasaheb Sarpotdar in 1935; the Times of India notes its links with Dadasaheb Phalke's film circle.

sources.label: Times of India: Tracing Pune's oldest cafes

shops.name: Chitale Bandhu Mithaiwale
shops.known_for: Bhakarwadi - the snack that made a Pune dairy a global brand.
shops.note: The Chitale family business traces to a 1939 dairy; the Bajirao Road shop made bhakarwadi a Pune signature, as The Print recounts.

shops.name: Kayani Bakery
shops.known_for: Shrewsbury biscuits, mawa cakes and bread - queues are part of the ritual.
shops.note: Opened in August 1955 by the Kayani brothers, who had migrated from Iran; the Indian Express profiles it as a city heritage landmark.

shops.name: Budhani Bros Waferwala
shops.known_for: Potato wafers fried in-house since before the packaged-chip era.
shops.note: DNA traces the family shop from a kadhai and kerosene stove in 1955 to an automated line, still a city icon.

shops.name: Marz-o-rin
shops.known_for: Sandwiches, cold coffee and plum cake in a heritage building.
shops.note: Sheriar Sheriyarji opened it on 11 February 1965 with four items; the family tells the story on its site, and the Indian Express profiles the founders.

shops.name: Sujata Mastani
shops.known_for: Mastani - Pune's thick milkshake-dessert; the rose flavour came first.
shops.note: Sharadrao Kondhalkar started the shop in 1967; India Today records the original 80-paise rose mastani. The drink's name nods to Mastani of Peshwa-era fame, as the Indian Express explains.

shops.name: Vohuman Cafe
shops.known_for: Cheese omelette, bun maska and Irani chai.
shops.note: Hormuz Irani opened it on 15 August 1978; Sahapedia and the Indian Express both record the story.

sources.label: Indian Express: Pune on my plate

shops.name: Laxminarayan Chivda
shops.known_for: The city's signature chivda - poha, peanuts, copra and raisins.
shops.note: Founded by hawker-turned-merchant Laxminarayan Data; published accounts place the founding in the early 1900s but differ on the exact year, so no "since" date is claimed here.

sources.label: Indian Express: Pune's most-loved chiwda brand
